title: Every Real Estate Lead Asks These 3 Questions. Answer Them First
seoTitle: Every Real Estate Lead Asks These 3 Questions
description: Every condo lead asks the same 3 questions: window direction, what is across the street, and when the keys come. Answer them before they ask.

body:
A new lead fills in your form. Your team calls, sends a brochure, and waits. Then the lead replies with a question. And then another one. In my experience, it is almost always the same questions, from almost every buyer. So why are you still waiting for them to ask?

## The 3 questions every lead asks

When someone is thinking about buying a condo, especially one that is not built yet, the questions on their mind are simple and personal:

1. **Which way do my windows face?** Light, view and privacy all start here. A buyer wants to picture the morning sun or the evening view from their own unit, not from a rendering of the top floor.
2. **What is across the street?** A park, a busy road, another tower, an empty lot. This is what they will look at every single day.
3. **When do I get my keys?** Timing decides everything else: when they move, when they can rent it out, how long their money is waiting.

None of these are tricky questions. They are the questions that sit between interest and a decision.

## Why waiting for the question costs you

Every time a lead has to ask, there is a pause. They wait for a reply, maybe they forget, maybe they look at another project in the meantime. If the answer takes a day, the doubt has a day to grow. A question you already know is coming is a question you should have answered already.

## Where to answer them

Put the answers where the buyer meets you first:

- **In a post.** Show the view by direction, the street around the building, and the delivery timeline.
- **On the website.** Make each answer easy to find for every unit, not hidden behind a form or a call.
- **In the first email.** Do not open with a generic thank you. Open with the three answers for the unit they looked at.

## What value first really means

Value first is not a slogan. It means you give the buyer what they need before they have to ask for it. You are not chasing them with follow-ups and reminders. You are already helping them make a decision.

That changes the relationship. The lead stops feeling like a target and starts feeling like someone you understand. And a buyer who feels understood is much easier to talk to when the time comes to sign.

So look at your own funnel today. Which of these three questions does your website answer right now? If the answer is none, you know where to start.
